post.caption: Japan's ama divers whistle when they surface. Their whistle, isobue, made Japan's list of 100 soundscapes in 1996. Ama diving is said to be about 2,000 years old. One dive lasts about a minute and reaches around 20 meters. Many ama still decline air tanks, partly to avoid overfishing. Abalone is their most important catch. In 1893 Kokichi Mikimoto first succeeded in growing pearls. Ama brought up the oysters and put them back after seeding. Mikimoto Pearl Island opened in 1951 with daily ama dives. In 2017 Japan named ama diving an important folk cultural property.
